newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kinshasa, Brazzaville exchange shell fire -radio.
newsitem.headline: Kinshasa, Brazzaville exchange shell fire -radio.

text.p: Troops fired shells from Kinshasa into neighbouring Congo Brazzaville in retaliation for firing from there, state radio in Kinshasa said on Thursday.
"Shells from Brazzaville fell on Tuesday on the seminary...leaving two wounded, including a little girl seriously," La Voix du Peuple radio said.
"The Democratic Republic of the Congo (former Zaire) retaliated towards the Bacongo and Makelekele districts of Brazzaville," the radio added.

Brazzaville, the capital of the Congo Republic, has been the scene of bloody fighting since June between political factions allied to President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguessou. Brazzaville lies across the Congo River from Kinshasa.
Kinshasa radio did not say which side fired the shells from Brazzaville, but a Brazzaville-based radio station controlled by Lissouba on Wednesday blamed forces loyal to Sassou.
An uneasy truce in Brazzaville has been disturbed by exchanges of fire in recent days, and further shelling inside the capital was heard on Thursday.
